html:
On 29 May 1953 Edmund Hillary of New Zealand and Tenzing Norgay, a Sherpa, became the first people known to reach the summit of Mount Everest, on the border of Nepal and Tibet.

They were part of a British expedition led by John Hunt that climbed from the Nepal side, which had opened to foreigners only a few years before. Earlier British attempts had come from Tibet; on one of them, in 1924, George Mallory and Andrew Irvine disappeared near the top. News of the climb reached London on the morning of the queen's coronation.

The ascent made Tenzing a hero across South Asia and made the Sherpa people famous as climbers. Mountaineering and trekking became a major business for Nepal, and Hillary spent decades building schools and clinics in the Khumbu region below the mountain.
sum: On 29 May 1953 Edmund Hillary of New Zealand and Tenzing Norgay, a Sherpa, became the first people known to reach the summit of Mount Everest, on the border of Nepal and Tibet.
